reason: The cited evidence shows that amorphization (E1) and grain refinement (E2) can occur in HEAs, and that CoCrFeNiMo alloys resist corrosion (E3), but none demonstrates the core causal chain: that mechanical stress dynamically induces nanostructuring which then drives self-healing passivation and simultaneous wear-corrosion resistance. The key mechanistic link is unsupported.
premises: Mechanical stress induces dynamic grain refinement and/or amorphization in HEAs
This refined/amorphized surface promotes rapid formation and repair of a protective passive oxide layer
The self-adaptive layer reduces both wear and corrosion simultaneously
The mechanism operates in CoCrFeNiMo-based HEAs under tribocorrosion in NaCl solution
Pre-conditioning or processing can trigger this adaptive nanostructuring
